findings.reason: a node taking the gloss as a mapping reserves `outcome` and not `top`, so an append anchored `top` passes the refusal, and the next synthesis, which writes `top`, folds that anchor into the rendered section — exactly the loss §4 exists to prevent; s4's ninth case (both sides read one set off the plan's comment keys) stays green under that mapping because both sides move together on the wrong id.
findings.text: s4 states the rendered set contains `outcome` for the plan-level key ("with the plan-level key `_top` rendered as `outcome` (near lines 70, 340–354 and 372)"), but `_render_document` normalises comment keys through `_section_key` first (`comments_by_section` at evidence.py:340–343), and `_section_key("_top")` returns `"top"`, so the `key == "_top"` branches at evidence.py:371–372 are unreachable and a plan-level comment section is written as `<section id="top">`. Verified by rendering a plan whose comments are keyed `_top`: the emitted section is `<section id="top">`, and `_section_key('_top')` prints `'top'`

findings.reason: the `<pre>`/`<code>` exclusion is existing behaviour s3 states it preserves rather than builds, and the node still declares four working controls, so adding a fifth changes the evidence record without changing what the node builds.
findings.text: s3's fifth case ("a spelling inside `<code>` is neither reported nor refused") has no negative control among the four declared; the controls cover cases one and two (one-spelling regex), case three (followup op sites and `append_to_list`) and case four (bare `§N`), so the exemption is the single assertion in the done-when whose mutation is never demonstrated, even though the exemption lives in `_prose_text` (doccheck.py:385–404) which the widened reader shares

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_DEFERRED_WORK_TERM` (doccheck.py:419), `_prose_deferred_work_term` (_store.py:993), the comment branch of `_apply_append` (_store.py:3798), the followups append op (_store.py:3757–3776), `append_to_list` (_store.py:2381), the `followups.<id>.<field>` set (_store.py:3482), `mcp_edit_plan.py:253`, `_section_key`/`available` (evidence.py:50, 353), `_evidence_record_path` (_store.py:1172), `_apply_evidence_appends` (_store.py:1230), `_evidence_section_html` (_store.py:1197), `EvidenceSynthesisResult` (evidence.py:24) and `synthesize_evidence` (project_maintenance_commands.py:1473) all resolve, each within a few lines of the cited number.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — every measure in s4 names a control that covers it, but s3's fifth case (the `<code>`/`<pre>` exemption) is the one assertion among its five that no listed negative control falsifies.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections require every log under the run directory, opening with its revision and the literal command and closing on `EXIT=`, which is a durable path a later reader can open.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `lost_anchors`, `data-evidence-origin`, the `dropped`/`replaced`/`retired`/`carried` tags and both test module names describe the mechanism; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or changelog prose reaches them.
rubric_items.reasoning: two findings — s3's claim that the warning and the refusal widen together does not hold for the other prose surfaces the audit reads, and s4 names a rendered id (`outcome`) that `_render_document` does not write.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s3 is one deliverable (widen the term and enforce it at the body-writing sites) and s4 is one (carry appended anchors and name each loss), with every case hanging off a set derived by one function.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` declares s3 waiting on s2 and s4 on s2 and s3, which matches the shared `reckon/_store.py` write each section names, and the open followup orders the same three sections.
